openings.claim: Join coloured tray tags identifying material types with completed samples showing pattern contents at a sample-to-tag pick ledger: pencil the assigned pattern and sample-derived material-tag/count pairs on each envelope, then tally each transfer before closure. This could make omissions detectable during filling.
openings.delta: The interface binds a pattern's required quantity to the tag identifying the selected material and the actual envelope transfer; merely displaying both parents leaves that binding implicit.
openings.prediction: Under matched pattern mixtures, the bound ledger will reduce shared-material omissions more than unlinked tags plus samples, while exposing any time cost. Pattern notation may also prevent envelope exchanges; neither benefit is established.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is loose materials beside each volunteer, suggested by O4. If crossing and shared access cause omissions, local staging will outperform the ledger, and binding tags to samples will add little after reach counts are controlled.
openings.defeat: Matched comparisons showing no omission advantage over unlinked parents defeat the interaction claim; inability to finish all 60 within 90 minutes or fit the table defeats intervention suitability.
openings.probe: Within the two-volunteer, 90-minute assembly, counterbalance small matched-pattern blocks across baseline, each parent alone, unlinked parents, and hybrid. Count omissions, corrections, reaches and minutes, including setup/checking. Keep quantities/dimensions fixed and all supplies on the existing table. This bounded comparison offers screening evidence; it cannot establish full-run hybrid performance.
assumptions: Sample contents can be read accurately enough to derive quantities and dimensions.
Envelope ledgers and samples fit alongside supplies on the existing table.
Required pattern assignments permit comparable blocks; O4's mixture is unknown.

component_comparison.baseline: Unlabelled trays without samples: predict selection and quantity errors under the same constraints.
component_comparison.parent_a: Tags alone: predict better material identification, residual pattern-quantity omissions.
component_comparison.parent_b: Samples alone: predict better quantity reference, residual selection/transfer omissions.
component_comparison.hybrid: Predict fewer shared-material transfer omissions through explicit sample/tag/count binding.
component_comparison.interaction_test: Against identical requirements, compare hybrid with unlinked parents and each alone; require a binding-specific omission reduction, not just their separate benefits. Record time and footprint failures.
